analysis.file_name: Novartis (NOVN.S)_ Takeaways from our Multiple Sclerosis KOL call following remibrutinib data presentation at MSToronto 2026.pdf
analysis.title: Novartis (NOVN.S): Takeaways from our Multiple Sclerosis KOL call following remibrutinib data presentation at MSToronto 2026
key_insights: GS rates Novartis Sell with a 12m target of SFr113 (NOVN.S) and $136 (NVS ADR), 11.7% and 10.0% below the 23 Oct close of SFr128 and $151.12.

GS says the remibrutinib REMODEL-1/2 data missed the bar its investor conversations set: an ARR benefit above 40% and a 6-month CDP-EDSS benefit of 34-45%. Reported were an ARR benefit of 31-35% and a 6-month CDP-EDSS of 29.2%.

NVS ADR closed down 3.3% versus RHHBY ADR up 2.6% on 23 October. GS expects NOVN shares to underperform the ADR move slightly more, and sees risk/reward skewed to the downside at +0% to +2% versus -5% to -7% (previously balanced at +/-3-4%).

Novartis guided to remibrutinib peak sales of $4bn+ in RMS (upside in SPMS, GSe $3bn) and $4bn+ in CSU/CIndU (GSe $3.5bn), above $8bn in total. GSe total is $9.5bn, or $7.6bn at 80% probability of success. GS notes many investors already assume up to $10bn.

The two KOLs called BTKi efficacy in MS moderate. They saw fenebrutinib (Roche) with an efficacy edge and remibrutinib with a safety edge, and expect slow uptake in relapsing MS (RMS) where anti-CD20 drugs dominate.
KOLs see BTKi use in 5-10% of RMS patients and 15-33% of progressive MS patients (PPMS and SPMS). Both would use the drugs off-label in PPMS and SPMS.
GS forecasts a BTKi MS market of about $7.5bn (about 25% of the MS market): $4.5bn fenebrutinib ($1.5bn PPMS, $3bn RMS) and $3bn remibrutinib. It assumes a 50:50 share in RMS.

KOLs flagged a theoretical concern that covalent BTK inhibition could raise BTK expression over time and wane efficacy after the first 6 months. They also wanted benefit shown over 1-2 years and were sceptical that nominal significance came only on a pooled basis.
Liver toxicity is the key class safety issue. KOLs see remibrutinib's liver profile as attractive but early, and see liver monitoring for fenebrutinib as inconvenient but not a barrier to use.

Suicidality was not seen as a class effect. Remibrutinib's presentation reported two deaths, one a suicide. FENhance 1/2 reported one confirmed and one suspected suicide. One KOL put approval odds at about 60/40 and the other expects both drugs approved.

GS argues one extra suicide in the fenebrutinib RMS trials does not show higher suicide risk. It says the REMODEL statistical plan targeted a 45% ARR benefit and 40% CDP-EDSS benefit, so the investigators aimed higher than what was achieved.

Novartis plans filings by end 2026 using a Priority Review Voucher. It sees US target pools of about 30% of 40k naive patients, 40% of 60k oral patients at risk of failure, and 45% of 140k anti-CD20 patients eligible to sequence. GS flags that switching is untested until the RESHAPE study reads out in 2028.

The remibrutinib HS readout is expected in Q4 2026 with first filing in 2027. The food allergy Phase 3 started in Q3 2026 with a readout after 2029. MFN pricing applies only to the Medicaid channel, about 10%.

GS says Novartis' 2026 scorecard does not support the share price. It lists 4Q25 and 1Q26 revenue misses, a low-quality 2Q26 beat, three Phase 3 misses (HORIZON, HARBOR, VAYHIA), REMODEL 1/2 below expectations and a paused YTB323 programme. NOVN is up 16.8% YTD versus EU Pharma up 4.7%, about 12% outperformance GS calls unjustified.
GS 3Q26 results are imminent and GS expects them in line with consensus. Valuation uses a 50:50 blend of DCF (CHF111, WACC 7.1%, TGR 1%) and 13.5x 2027E EPS (CHF114).

market_movers.rationale: GS sees too much credit given for remibrutinib in MS, neutral earnings momentum and a pipeline record that does not justify 12% sector outperformance.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees Novartis' roughly 12% YTD outperformance versus EU Pharma as unjustified given mixed results and Phase 3 misses, with multiple expansion ahead of loss-of-exclusivity waves.

earnings_insights: GS expects 3Q26 results to be in line with consensus (GSe in line with cons), results imminent as of 26 October 2026.
GS estimates 2026E EPS of $8.85 (down 0.7% from $8.91 reported in 2025), 2027E $9.83 and 2028E $10.44. These are GS estimates, not reported figures.
GS estimates quarterly EPS of $2.22 for 9/26E, $2.27 for 12/26E and $2.21 for 3/27E, with $2.40 listed for 6/26.
GS 2026E revenue is $56,571.7mn (+3.7%) and EBIT $21,848.1mn versus $21,889.0mn in 2025. GS flags 2026E acquisitions of $13,053mn.
Prior 2026 results per GS: 4Q25 revenue miss, 1Q26 revenue and operating profit miss, 2Q26 low-quality beat.
risk_factors: Upside risks to the GS Sell: ongoing positive earnings momentum, stronger-than-expected sales from key franchises, unexpected pipeline success, and capital allocation including BD and buybacks.
Liver toxicity is a class risk for BTK inhibitors, and there is no safety data for BTKi use after CD20 therapy.
Switching from anti-CD20 drugs is untested until the RESHAPE readout in 2028.
Possible waning of covalent BTKi efficacy after 6 months due to BTK upregulation, which KOLs called a theoretical concern.
Approval risk: one KOL put approval odds at about 60/40.
vol_and_positioning: GS frames the NOVN risk/reward ahead of MSToronto as +0% to +2% upside versus -5% to -7% downside, previously balanced at +/-3-4%, with the shares about 3% below the post-remibrutinib-MS, pre-pelacarsen and del-desiran price.
geopolitical: Remibrutinib CSU pricing is subject to the US MFN agreement only in the Medicaid channel, about 10% of volume, which GS says is already assumed in peak sales guidance.

tension_points.bull_case: Novartis guides to $4bn+ peak sales in RMS, sees safety with no liver monitoring as the differentiator and cites large switch and oral-eligible pools. GS notes many investors already see up to $10bn.
tension_points.bear_case: KOLs call efficacy moderate, expect 5-10% RMS use, see CD20 drugs staying dominant, and the data missed investor ARR and CDP-EDSS expectations. GS says the shares still give too much credit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A liver monitoring requirement on the fenebrutinib label that favours remibrutinib, or switching data. GS notes the RESHAPE switch study reads out in 2028.

theme_stances.key_argument: The REMODEL data missed investor expectations, so there is still too much credit given for remibrutinib in MS.
